text: Corruption of 匄. Its original meaning is unknown; perhaps it was "to damage".
From the clerical script (隸書) of 竝 (OC *beːŋʔ), originally depicting two people standing side-by-side.
According to Xu Shen, 𦫳 together with 𠔁.
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *prɯn, *bɯns): semantic 亻 + phonetic 分 (OC *pɯn, *bɯns).
人 (“person”) + 止 (“foot”) – a person standing on tiptoes.
Ideogrammic compound (會意 / 会意): ⺅ (“person”) + 戈 (“spear”). Based on the image of cutting a person’s neck with a spear, it expresses the meanings of "to cut off" or "to strike."
Multiple explanations. Most consider the character an Ideogrammic compound (會意 / 会意).

Uncertain. There are some hypotheses:
* Xu Zhongshu: Bottom half of 冓, pictogram (象形) of a fish, then drawn in a similar way to 丙 (perhaps a fish tail). See 魚 and 丙
* Shizuka Shirakawa：Pictogram (象形) of tools used for weaving ropes.
* Ji Xusheng: Ideogrammic compound (會意 / 会意): 魚 (“fish”) + 二 (“two”) – to catch two fish at once (kill two birds with one stone). Compare the oracle bone script form of 亟.
* Xu Shen: Ideogrammic compound (會意 / 会意): 一 (“one”) + abbreviated 冓 – to catch two fish at once.
* Ideogrammic compound (會意 / 会意): 一 + 冓 (“the shape of a basket repeatedly woven from bamboo”). It signifies the concept of repeating something that was once done, conveying the meaning of "again."
* ↑ 1.0 1.1 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「再」
Originally 皇. A spurious 𠘨 was added by the assimilation with 鳳.
Variant of 刀 (dāo).
Variant of 句, via 口 → 厶.
Omission of 彳 in 御. 午 (OC *ŋaːʔ) still gives the sound.

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *panʔ, *pʰan): semantic 又 (“hand”) + phonetic 厂 (OC *hŋaːnʔ, *hŋaːns). The character originally depicted the action of turning the palm of the hand, and by extension, it came to mean "to return" or "to reverse."

Inconclusive.
* Liú Xìnglóng interprets 刁 to be a hand instead.
* Táng Lán: Originally the same character as 后, which later diverged.
* Shuowen: 后 flipped.
A popular variant of 弔; an intermediate obsolete variant is 𨒝.

Ideogrammic compound (會意 / 会意): 戌 (“ax”) + 口 — to terminate. The 口 is a distinguishing mark. Later borrowed to mean "all".[字源 1]
Other explanations include shouting together with a spear in front of the battlefield, implying everyone; alternatively, to cut off one's head with an ax, depriving them of all they have; alternatively, to break a pot with an ax.
For etymology 2, simplified from 鹹 (elimination of 鹵). Cite error: <ref> tags exist for a group named "字源", but no corresponding <references group="字源"/> tag was found
Stacked form of 可 (OC *kʰaːlʔ), perhaps an open mouth with breath going out while talking or singing. In fact, the original meaning of 哥 and perhaps 可 was "to sing; song".
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *tjɯn, *ɦljun): phonetic 辰 (OC *djɯn) + semantic 口 (“mouth”).

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, *kˤraŋ): phonetic 庚 (*lˤaŋ) + semantic 口 (“mouth”). 口 functions as a differentiating mark (cf. 古/固), not as semantic "mouth." The graph abstracts some property — likely "hollowness" or "spatial openness" — from 庚, a pictograph of a hollow percussion/ritual instrument. Used in oracle bones for Shang king Cheng Tang.
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声): semantic 口 (“mouth”) + phonetic 啇.
The same character as 咢, both ultimately derived from or identical to 喪, see there for more.

Originally written 薶 (mái), a phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *mrɯː): semantic 艹 (“plant”) + phonetic 貍 (OC *p·rɯ).
Later changed to 埋, a phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *mrɯː): semantic 土 (“earth”) + phonetic 里 (OC *rɯʔ).
A shape variant of 柰 (Wang, 1996).

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声): semantic 女 (“female, woman”) + phonetic 也 (OC *laːlʔ).
Originally a variant of 姐 (jiě, “elder sister”). Later repurposed as a feminine third-person pronoun influenced by European languages, with the glyph being the result of replacing the 人 (rén, “person”) radical in 他 (tā) with 女 (“woman”). Linguist Liu Bannong is credited with coining this use around the 1910s, in turn replacing a precursor form of 他女 in print (Bi, 2013).
Corrupted form of 㜛.

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *l'ɯwɢs): semantic 宀 (“roof”) + phonetic 由 (OC *lɯw). It originally represented the farthest place accessible by boat or vehicle and, by extension, came to express the idea of spatial expansion or vastness.

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *sqʰon): semantic 宀 (“roof”) + phonetic 亘 (xuān). The character originally represented the main hall where the emperor resided. By extension, it came to be used to mean "clear" or "evident."
小 (“small”) + 大 (“large”) – the width of an object gradually changing from small to large.
Originally written 㞕.
May have originally been the same character as 巳, a pictogram (象形) of either a snake or a fetus. This character cannot be found in the Shuowen Jiezi.
Original form of 把.

合 + 手.
A later alternative glyph of 拏 and 挐 for senses related to “to take with hand”. Originally regarded as unorthodox by Zhengzitong and Zihui.

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *kʷreːs): semantic ⺘ (“hand”) + phonetic 卦 (OC *kʷreːs). It expresses the idea of hooking or hanging something with the hand. Originally, it was a popular form of the character 挂.
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *kʰroːŋ, *kʰoːŋs): semantic 扌 + phonetic 空 (OC *kʰoːŋ, *kʰoːŋs).
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *laŋ): semantic 手 (“hand”) + phonetic 昜 (OC *laŋ).

Ideogrammic compound (會意 / 会意): semantic 斤 (“axe”) + semantic 車 (“cart; vehicle”). It refers to an ancient punishment in which a body was torn apart using carts, and by extension, conveys the meaning “to cut.” Another theory expresses the idea of cutting wood to make a vehicle.
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *mɯːds): semantic 日 (“sun; day”) + phonetic 未 (OC *mɯds).
Variant of 綿 by replacing 糸 with 木 (裘錫圭：《文字學概要（修訂本）》, p222).
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *dul): semantic 木 (“tree”) + phonetic 隹 (OC *tjul). It expresses the idea of a piece of wood used to smash things, signifying a “hammer” or “mallet.”
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *kjub): semantic 氵 (“water”) + phonetic 十 (OC *ɡjub). It expresses the idea of a liquid.
Variant of 沈, see there for more.

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *lon): semantic 氵 (“water”) + phonetic 㕣 (OC *lon). The character originally referred to the edge of a river, and by extension, it came to represent the idea of "following along" or "accompanying."
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *kʰrɯb): semantic 氵 (“water”) + phonetic 立 (OC *rɯb). The character originally meant "tears," and by extension, it came to represent the act of "crying."

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *ŋreː, *ŋre) and ideogrammic compound (會意 / 会意): semantic 氵 (“water”) + phonetic 厓 (OC *ŋreː, “cliff; to limit”). It represents a cliff by the water, conveying the meaning “riverbank” or “shore.”
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *deːns): semantic 水 (“water”) + phonetic 定 (OC *teːŋs, *deːŋs)

畾 + 宜 – a pile.
Originally as 曡, with 晶 (jīng) on top. Shuowen commented that the shape change was promoted by the emperor of the short-lived Xin Dynasty, who deemed the use of three "suns" (日) in this character too empowering - compared to three "fields" (田).
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *l̥ʰoːŋs): semantic 疒 (“illness”) + phonetic 甬 (OC *loŋʔ). The character conveys the meaning of "pain" or "to hurt."
Triplication of 直 (“straight”).
Triplication of 石 (“stone”).

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *tkuːb): semantic 竹 (“bamboo”) + phonetic 合 (OC *kuːb, *ɡuːb). Originally, it was a variant of 荅, where the semantic component 艸 (grass) was later mistakenly replaced by 竹 (bamboo). It expresses the meaning of "to respond."
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *ʔsiːɡ): semantic ⺮ (“bamboo”) + phonetic 即 (OC *ʔsɯɡ). It represents the "node" of bamboo, and by extension, signifies a segment or boundary.
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *kreːnʔ): semantic 竹 + phonetic 間 (OC *ɡreːn)
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *tjunʔ, *djun): semantic 糸 (“thread”) + phonetic 屯 (OC *duːn, *tun). It conveys the meaning of "without any impurities," and also "exclusively."
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *menʔ): semantic 糸 (“silk”) + phonetic 面 (OC *mens).
Pictogram (象形). The component 戶 (representing the shape of a shoulder) is combined with 月 (the radical of 肉, meaning "flesh" or "meat") to convey the meaning of "shoulder."

Evolved geometrically from 胄 (*l'ɯwɢs) in Han dynasty era (Liu, 2023).
Before that, Pronunciation 1 was written as 毓; see there for more.

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *pruː, *pʰruː) and ideogrammic compound (會意 / 会意): semantic 月 (“flesh”) + phonetic 包 (OC *pruː, “a shape representing a pregnant figure”). It conveys the meaning of the membrane that encloses the fetus.
The proto-form of 盤 + 攴. The proto-form of 盤 was later corrupted into 舟, and 攴 evolved into 殳.
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *qrol, *qrols): semantic 艹 (“grass; plant”) + phonetic 委 (OC *qrol, *qrolʔ).

Duplication of 柰 (*naːds) or 祟 (*sqʰluds) (Guo, 2010b; Su, 2012).
See also 祘.
Originally written as 埶 (OC *ŋeds). The 艸 (“grass; plant”) and 云 were added later.
Unknown.
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *qʰuns): semantic 言 (“speech”) + phonetic 川 (OC *kʰjon). It conveys the meaning of "preaching a teaching."
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *kʰeːm): semantic 言 (“speech”) + phonetic 兼 (OC *keːm, *keːms). It expresses the state of being respectful or reverent.
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *njaŋs): semantic 言 + phonetic 襄 (OC *snaŋ) – to criticize; to reproach.
Possibly a variation of 壴 with the top part modified. May have been the original form of 凱 (“music of triumph”).
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *tʰeːb): semantic 貝 (“shell”) + phonetic 占 (OC *ʔljem, *tjems).
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *loŋʔ): semantic 𧾷 (“legs”) + phonetic 甬 (OC *loŋʔ)
Triplication of 車 (“cart”).

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *panʔ) and ideogrammic compound (會意 / 会意): semantic 辶 (“movement”) + phonetic 反 (OC *panʔ, *pʰan, “to return”). It originally conveyed the meaning of "to return along the path one came from" and, by extension, came to signify the idea of "to restore" or "to revert."
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *peːns): semantic 辶 (“walk; movement”) + phonetic 扁 (OC *pʰen, *benʔ, *peːnʔ, *beːnʔ).
Ideogrammic compound (會意 / 会意): 門 (“door”) + 木 (“wood”) – a fence.
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *kʰraɡ): semantic ⻖ (“mound”) + phonetic 𡭴. It expresses the idea of a hole or gap in a wall.
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 / 形声, OC *kʷaːs, *ɡʷaːʔ): phonetic 戶 (OC *ɡʷaːʔ) + semantic 隹.
